No rating: the sources are news reports and organiser statements, which describe how an event was run, not how runners rated it. A score needs participant evidence -- race reports, runner blogs, attributed quotes -- and without it would be invention.
title: Pontianak City Run 2027 Review: What the 2026 Edition Was Like
seo_title: Pontianak City Run 2027 Review | West Kalimantan Marathon
meta_description: Pontianak City Run review: about 6,000 runners in 2026, from Kenya, the Netherlands, Japan and Kuching. What that means for the 2027 race on 31 January.
dek: An equator-city race that drew around 6,000 runners in 2026 -- including from Kenya, the Netherlands, Japan and across the border in Kuching -- and one of very few with a full marathon on Indonesian Borneo.
verdict: Pontianak City Run has grown into a genuine regional destination race. The 2026 edition on Sunday 15 February drew around 6,000 runners [1], not only from West Kalimantan but from Jakarta, Surabaya, Makassar, Palembang and Bali, and internationally from Kuching, Kenya, the Netherlands and Japan [1]. The mayor described it as a draw for tourism, with runners arriving early and staying overnight [1]. Its rarest quality is the long category: a full marathon is unusual anywhere in Kalimantan, which makes this one of the few chances to run the distance on Indonesian Borneo.

sections.heading: The 2026 Edition
paragraphs: The 2026 race was held on Sunday 15 February in Pontianak, the capital of West Kalimantan, with around 6,000 runners taking part [1]. It offered 5 km, 10 km and 21 km categories alongside a long-distance category [1].
Pontianak sits almost exactly on the equator, which shapes everything about racing there: hot, humid conditions year-round and a very early start to beat the heat.

sections.heading: Who Came, and From Where
paragraphs: The field was notably wide. Beyond West Kalimantan itself, runners came from Jakarta, Surabaya, Makassar, Palembang and Bali, and from abroad -- Kuching across the Malaysian border, as well as Kenya, the Netherlands and Japan [1].

Kenyan entrants are usually a sign that a race offers prize money worth travelling for, and the Kuching contingent reflects how close Pontianak is to Malaysian Sarawak. Both suggest a front of the field that is genuinely competitive.

sections.heading: A Tourism Event as Much as a Race
paragraphs: Mayor Edi Rusdi Kamtono framed the event in economic terms: runners arriving early and staying overnight, with hotels, restaurants and small businesses benefiting [1]. He also tied it to promoting the city during the Lunar New Year and Cap Go Meh celebrations [1].

That timing matters to a visitor. Pontianak has one of Indonesia's larger Chinese-Indonesian communities, and Cap Go Meh there is a major festival. A race that coincides with it is a reason to stay longer, and a reason to book accommodation early.

sections.heading: What to Expect in 2027
paragraphs: The 2027 edition moves earlier, to Sunday 31 January, and is listed with 5 km, 10 km, a 21 km half marathon and a 42 km full marathon, with entry from Rp98,000 [2].

That is roughly two weeks earlier than 2026. Because the 2026 date was chosen partly around the Lunar New Year period [1], it is worth checking how the 2027 date sits against the festival calendar before planning a trip around both.

sections.heading: Should You Enter?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a full marathon on Indonesian Borneo -- there are very few -- or a well-attended race with an international front end in an under-visited city. The low entry price makes it one of the better-value events of its size.
Go in expecting equatorial conditions. The heat and humidity will cost you time, and a full marathon here is a test of pacing and hydration more than of speed.
This review is compiled from published reporting on the previous edition and the organisers' own announcements. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: How many people ran Pontianak City Run in 2026?
faqs.answer: Around 6,000 runners took part on Sunday 15 February 2026. They came from across West Kalimantan, from cities including Jakarta, Surabaya, Makassar, Palembang and Bali, and from abroad, including Kuching, Kenya, the Netherlands and Japan.

faqs.question: Why do international runners go to Pontianak City Run?
faqs.answer: It is one of very few races on Indonesian Borneo with a full marathon, and the presence of Kenyan and Dutch runners in 2026 points to a competitive front of the field. Kuching in Malaysian Sarawak is also close, which brings runners across the border.

faqs.question: What are conditions like at Pontianak City Run?
faqs.answer: Hot and humid. Pontianak sits almost exactly on the equator, so temperatures stay high year-round and the race starts very early to limit the heat. Expect it to cost you time, and treat the full marathon as a test of pacing and hydration.
